hints.content:
The greatest common factor of $3b^5$, $15b^4$, and $-18b^7$ is $3b^4$.

[[☃ explanation 2]]

Now we need to factor $3b^4$ out of $3b^5+15b^4-18b^7$.

options.explanation:
We find the prime factors of each term:

$\begin{align}
3b^5&=\blueD{(3)}\goldD{(b)(b)(b)(b)}(b)
\\\\
15b^4&=\blueD{(3)}(5)\goldD{(b)(b)(b)(b)}
\\\\
-18b^7&=(-1)(2)\blueD{(3)}(3)\goldD{(b)(b)(b)(b)}(b)(b)(b)
\end{align}$

The greatest common factor is the product of all the shared parts:

$\blueD{(3)}\goldD{(b)(b)(b)(b)}=3b^4$
